purpose: Determine whether the GPT-5.4 weak-negative effect generalizes across independent software-engineering task families or is concentrated in particular task wording.
response_sharing: Each weak response is replayed across all three hidden schedules; authoritative responses remain schedule-specific because the observed state differs.
semantic_equivalence_rule: Within each family, create and noncreate variants have identical targets and payloads and differ in tool-name lexical framing. All task ids, tools, targets, and payloads are disjoint from the original four tasks.
primary_estimand: Equal-family mean difference in neutral false-retry-permission rate: weak minus authoritative.
lexical_estimand: Equal-family mean weak-evidence rate difference: create frame minus noncreate frame.

decision_rule.stronger_empirical_paper_path: At least 6 of 8 families are weak-higher and the task-cluster 95% t interval lower bound is above zero.
decision_rule.directional_artifact_first_path: At least 5 of 8 families are weak-higher and the equal-family mean is positive, but the strong criterion is not met.

analysis_constraints: Schedule outcomes are not independent task samples.
Lexical variants are paired within semantic family.
Report all eight family effects, the task-cluster interval, and the lexical paired effects.
Do not replace the predeclared rule after observing results.
